baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three q-w-l turns at words 1, 7, and 9 frame the question, the admission bala, and the reply.
baseline_models.mechanism: A negotiated speech sequence converts carried, manifest evidence into the addressees' own concession; the final command follows a fact that their answer has put on record.

activation_trace.role: Mutual speaking and negotiation make the three turns a compact evidentiary colloquy.
The carrier and carried message supply the evidence-bearing party recalled by the question.
Manifest disclosure makes the admitted fact one of prior clarity, not unavailable notice.
Denial of disclosed truth names the issue that the answer bala can no longer contest.

changed_reading.before: The guards remind the addressees that messengers came, and the addressees agree.
changed_reading.after: The three-turn exchange converts once-denied clear evidence into the disbelievers' own on-record admission before their plea is dismissed.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The ayah opposes ta'tikum and rusulukum at words 4-5 to id'u and du'a at words 10 and 12, ending with fi dalal at word 16.
baseline_models.mechanism: Evidence has an inbound route and carrier that successfully reaches the addressees, whereas their outbound call is described through deviation and loss as lacking a viable return route.

activation_trace.role: Arrival and reaching establish the successful inbound movement of evidence.
A messenger carrying speech supplies the inbound channel and its bearer.
Calling by speech supplies the attempted outbound movement in both command and noun.
Deviation from guidance and intended course turns failed response into a routing failure.
Loss of an object sharpens the image of a call that cannot be located at its destination.

changed_reading.before: The disbelievers' prayer is simply ineffective.
changed_reading.after: The ayah draws a directional asymmetry: truth reached them by an arriving carrier, but their answering call now has no viable route to its intended destination.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Bayyinat at word 6, al-kafirin at word 13, and dalal at word 16 form a disclosure-covering-disappearance sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: What was exposed and distinguishable is met by covering denial; the later call consequently enters hiddenness rather than producing a new disclosure.

activation_trace.role: Appearance and disclosure make the prior signs perceptibly open.
Covering supplies the material reversal applied to what had been made clear.
Hiddenness and disappearance provide the resulting state of the later call.
The voiced call is the item that passes from attempted expression into disappearance.

changed_reading.before: Their religious status explains why their supplication fails.
changed_reading.after: The status is rendered as an information sequence: what arrived exposed was covered over, so the later emitted call enters concealment rather than disclosure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus question compresses a formula repeatedly enacted across the surah: messengers and clear proofs arrive, a resistant response follows, and the final dialogue reduces all former defenses to the single concession bala.

activation_trace.role: The three negotiated turns are the compressed replay's question-and-answer frame.
Manifest evidence is the focus anchor shared with the repeated chains.
The earlier arrival supplies the same successful approach expressed in the focus question.
The message carrier reproduces the focus ayah's named source of notice.
The same manifest-proof branch makes 40:22 a near-verbatim precursor.
Explicit denial supplies the omitted response that the focus's label al-kafirin recalls.
A second messenger occurrence near the close reopens the same carried-message sequence.
Repeated manifest proofs show that the focus question summarizes a surah-wide pattern.
Knowledge disclosed to its possessor supplies the competing store in which they rejoice instead of receiving the proofs.

structural_cues: 40:22 reproduces kana plus ta'ti plus rusul plus bayyinat and immediately adds fa-kafaru.
40:83 repeats rusul plus bayyinat near the surah's end, then places the recipients with the knowledge already in their possession.
The focus asks only whether the repeated chain occurred and receives an unqualified bala.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two close repetitions and their resistant responses; I infer that the focus question functions as a compressed replay or checksum of that history. A live alternative is that the repetition only reinforces notice without giving the dialogue a formal recap function.

changed_reading.before: The question recalls one past encounter with messengers.
changed_reading.after: The question is the terminal compression of a repeatedly narrated evidence-response chain, and bala collapses the surah's many defenses into self-confirmation.

context_deltas.mechanism: The condemned first try to transfer their petition to custodians; after settled judgment, the keepers return the act with fa-id'u. Earlier aligned protective petition and the explicit absence of an obeyed intercessor show that mediation is relational and procedural, not a technique available on demand.

activation_trace.role: Covering sin and protecting its bearer supplies an earlier other-directed petition aligned with faith and return.
An advocate joined to another supplies the explicitly unavailable proxy role for wrongdoers.
Judgment between people fixes the procedural state before the request to the keepers.
The keeper defined by custody, not advocacy, is the requested prayer proxy.
The inmates direct a spoken call-command to the custodians and ask them to relay it.
Lightening a burden specifies the narrowly delegated relief sought through the proxy.
The reply returns both the act and its failed result to the original petitioners.

structural_cues: 40:49 directly supplies the ellipsed request: the people in the fire ask the keepers to call their Lord for one day's reduction.
40:47-48 first shows followers seeking relief from former superiors, who answer that all are together under a judgment already made.
The pronoun movement from rabbakum in 40:49 to fa-id'u in 40:50 shifts agency from your Lord through us back to you.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a failed ladder from followers to leaders to keepers, plus earlier petition and unavailable intercession; I infer that fa-id'u rejects outsourced relation and reallocates agency. It may alternatively be only a dismissive imperative, without a general principle of non-transferability.

changed_reading.before: The guards tell the prisoners to pray for themselves because prayer will fail.
changed_reading.after: Custodians refuse to become advocacy proxies after judgment and return the call to those who had outsourced the relation they previously refused.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated d-a-w occurrences create a routing network: a call to faith is refused, calls beside God have no adjudicative power, reciprocal calls lead toward rescue or fire, God states an explicit call-response relation, and former invoked objects later disappear. The focus call fails within that inverted network rather than because calling is intrinsically futile.

activation_trace.role: The command and noun anchor the changed reading in the focus's attempted spoken call.
Loss supplies the focus endpoint against which the surah's other call routes are compared.
The earlier call bends speech toward faith and is met by covering denial.
Calling other addressees supplies the alternate outbound route.
Otherness marks the alternate route as directed beside the stated judge.
Decisive judgment contrasts God's adjudication with the invoked others' inability to adjudicate anything.
Reciprocal calls show that the same speech act can incline hearers toward opposed destinations.
Rescue by separation names one destination of the opposed invitations.
The called-toward object is stated to possess no effective call in either temporal domain.
The direct imperative to call supplies the positive side of the call relation.
Returning speech and answering explicitly completes the positive call-response circuit.
The speakers deny their former calling after its addressees are reported missing.
The vanished invoked objects literalize one pole of lostness while the repeated root extends disappearance into disorientation.

structural_cues: 40:12 and 40:14 contrast refusal when God alone is called with the command to call sincerely.
40:41-43 stages opposed invitations toward rescue and fire and then denies efficacy to the rival called-toward object.
40:60 states call Me and I answer you, preventing the focus from being read as a blanket denial of call-response.
40:74 joins former invocation, disappearance, denial of having invoked anything, and the same d-l-l root.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated d-a-w nodes, destinations, and one explicit answer; I infer a coherent routing network whose history determines the focus failure. A live alternative is that these are distinct uses of calling and only the immediate 40:49-50 exchange controls the focus.

changed_reading.before: The prayer is lost because no prayer from these speakers can work.
changed_reading.after: The prayer is the terminal output of an inverted call network: they refused the call that reached them, routed calls elsewhere, and now find the return channel they seek absent.

context_deltas.mechanism: Confession, decisive judgment, witness, and the non-benefit of excuse turn the focus exchange into post-judgment evidentiary closure. Bala is not new information for the guards; it is self-witness that removes the last factual premise for relief.

activation_trace.role: Negotiated speech anchors the judicially changed reading in the focus's three formal turns.
Manifest evidence supplies the proposition to which the speakers attest.
Confession as acknowledgment and submission supplies an earlier self-incriminating speech act tied to a request for exit.
Decisive judgment establishes the surah's contrast between true adjudication and powerless substitutes.
Judgment between the servants immediately precedes the appeal to the keepers.
Presence with witnessing supplies the public evidentiary setting named just after the focus.
Denied benefit makes the later excuse procedurally fruitless.
The excuse supplies the class of post-judgment speech into which the focus plea can now be heard.

structural_cues: 40:11 pairs confession of sins with a question about any route out.
40:47-50 moves through appeals to leaders, judgment already rendered, appeal to keepers, and the focus's factual question.
40:51-52 immediately names the standing of witnesses and the failure of wrongdoers' excuse to benefit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies legal and testimonial vocabulary around the dialogue; I infer that the guards ask for an admission that closes rather than investigates the record. The alternative is a rhetorical moral reminder with no procedural force.

changed_reading.before: Bala is a simple acknowledgment before an unanswered request.
changed_reading.after: Bala functions as self-witness after judgment, converting the plea into a non-beneficial excuse rather than reopening the merits.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah distinguishes a receptive interval, marked by forgiveness, acceptance, and return, from speech produced only after manifest evidence and then witnessed force. The focus call is therefore not merely at the wrong destination; it is made after its evidence-responsive window has closed.

activation_trace.role: Past occurrence and temporal presence place the messengers' arrival in an earlier phase.
Prior arrival marks the event to which a timely response could have attached.
The present call is the temporally displaced response contrasted with prior arrival.
Covering sin while protecting its bearer supplies the surah's open side of reception.
Acceptance with satisfaction establishes that return can be received rather than intrinsically rejected.
Habitual return supplies the responsive posture linked there to remembering the signs.
The carried message reappears at the late historical boundary before punishment is seen.
Manifest proof fixes the earlier disclosure to which the late speakers failed to respond.
Seeing with the eye marks the later phase in which declarative belief is finally voiced.
The explicit absence of benefit after sight supplies the temporal closure.
General loss names the settled result at the point where late belief no longer benefits.

structural_cues: 40:3 places forgiving and accepting return beside severe consequence and final destination.
40:83-85 orders clear-proof arrival, sight of force, a new declaration of belief, and an explicit statement that this late belief did not benefit.
The focus itself orders past messenger arrival before the present imperative to call.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies open reception language and an explicit late-belief non-benefit sequence; I infer a phase boundary between response to evidence and speech after witnessed consequence. The live alternative is that speaker identity alone, rather than timing, explains the focus's lost prayer.

changed_reading.before: The call misses because its route or addressee is wrong.
changed_reading.after: The call is also lost in time: correct-sounding speech after the evidentiary window cannot retroactively become the response that the arriving proofs required.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it hears prayer tactically rather than devotionally. It remains anchored because 40:25 and 40:50 use the same wa-ma X al-kafirin illa fi dalal frame, while 40:37 supplies a second failed-plot frame; render it as a syntactic and functional echo, not as lexical identity or a claim that prayer in general is plotting.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The nominal closure wa-ma du'a'u al-kafirina illa fi dalalin, anchored in d-a-w at words 10 and 12, k-f-r at word 13, and d-l-l at word 16.

activation_trace.role: Plotting and contrivance occupy the same grammatical slot later occupied by the focus prayer.
The identical disbeliever class binds the failed plot formula to the focus formula.
The identical exclusive endpoint in deviation supplies the strongest formal bridge.
A second contrivance enters the repeated wa-ma X illa fi Y failure mold.
Ruin and loss provide the alternate failed endpoint of the repeated plotting mold.
The focus substitutes voiced petition for plotting in the same failure-shaped frame.
The same denying agents preserve continuity across the tactical and devotional modes.
The repeated deviation endpoint makes the prayer look like the last maneuver in an unchanged trajectory.

changed_reading.before: A devotional plea receives no effective answer.
changed_reading.after: Within the surah's repeated failure formula, prayer becomes the disbelievers' final maneuver after coercive plots fail: the speech mode changes, but its trajectory does not.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it activates the packet's secondary d-a-a mapping for the focus d-a-w root. It remains anchored to the exact fa-id'u imperative and is reinforced by the keeper, dragging, and stoking sequence; render it only as a pragmatic and material undertone of rebuff, never as the lexical translation of id'u.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Fa-id'u at word 10, resolved through the packet's secondary mapped root root_000477 while retaining the source root d-a-w.

activation_trace.role: The keeper as custodian supplies the institutional voice from which the following pushback comes.
The inmates' literal call-command establishes what the keepers pragmatically throw back at them.
The secondary branch's violent push gives fa-id'u an exploratory undertone of custodial shove or rebuff.
Deviation supplies the direction into which the rebuffed action is sent.
A restraint fixed around the body materializes the custodial setting of constrained movement.
Dragging and extending continue the material motion suggested by the secondary push branch.
Stoking and intensifying fire supplies the destination of the carceral motion.

changed_reading.before: Fa-id'u is a neutral permission or command to attempt prayer.
changed_reading.after: As a contained secondary activation, fa-id'u carries custodial pushback: the requested proxy action is shoved back onto the prisoners and into the same carceral motion.

strongest_changes: The focus dialogue became a self-closing evidentiary recap of the messenger and clear-proof chain repeated at 40:22 and 40:83.
The lost prayer became a route-specific failure within a surah-wide network of refused calls, rival calls, explicit response, and vanished invoked objects.
The immediate 40:49 request made fa-id'u a refusal of delegated prayer after judgment rather than a general statement that prayer cannot be answered.
The 40:83-85 sequence made the prayer temporally lost: it is voiced after the evidence-responsive window has closed.
The exact 40:25 and 40:50 failure frames activated the contained reading of prayer as the disbelievers' last failed maneuver.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet did not merely add themes; it exposed repeated verbal circuits and exact syntactic molds. Most distinctive were the positive call-answer statement at 40:60 against the lost call at 40:50, the proxy ladder immediately before the focus, and the substitution of du'a for kayd inside an otherwise repeated failure formula.
remaining_uncertainties: Dalal may support a directional routing image more strongly than a literal non-arrival of speech.
The shared failure frame securely marks analogy, but the tactical reading of prayer should not erase the possibility of sincere late distress.
The secondary d-a-a activation is intentionally exploratory and may carry only pragmatic texture rather than interpretive weight.
The legal vocabulary supports evidentiary closure, but the exact procedural force assigned to bala remains reader inference.
